summary:
We developed an engaging, school-age-friendly storytelling showcase titled "Abandoned But Not Forgotten," highlighting NASA's historic hardware resting across the Moon, Mars, and deep space.
Through vivid visual storytelling and accessible summaries, the project introduces young space enthusiasts to iconic pioneers—from the Moon’s Apollo Lunar Modules, Lunar Roving Vehicles, ALSEP instruments, and Surveyor landers, to Mars’s Viking, Phoenix, and InSight landers, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, and the Ingenuity helicopter, alongside deep-space travelers like Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer 10 & 11, and the Kepler Space Telescope. Rather than treating these machines as forgotten space debris, each profile brings their engineering purpose and groundbreaking scientific discoveries to life.
This project matters because every silent rover, lander, and probe represents humanity’s curiosity and resilience. Preserving their stories inspires the next generation of explorers to understand how past missions laid the foundation for future space discovery.
details: This project titled Abandoned But Not Forgotten is created using Canva and it tells the story of human-made things left behind in space, on the Moon and on Mars, like old satellites, rovers, landers, flags and tools, and it explains what they are, why they were left and what happened to them through simple visual storytelling. Most people think space is empty and clean, but in reality humans have left a lot of waste in space, on the Moon and on Mars, and this abandoned debris creates pollution and danger for future missions, while at the same time people are not aware that these forgotten objects are also a part of our human heritage and history. No coding languages were used for this project and only Canva software was used, as this is a non-coding, design-based awareness project where posters, infographics and timelines were designed to make a complex space topic easy to understand.
